chapter: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: The one owned-fleet figure to quote: (c) ~$0.0033 per request (≈$3.33 per 1K) — owned fleet, hour-matched active-hours basis, 6-host average at the ~10 rps average.
issue: The prose calls ~$0.0033/request (≈$3.33/1K) 'the one owned-fleet figure to quote', but the same chapter later quotes ~$49.13/1K for the 21-host peak fleet and ~$0.0029/request for the 21-host full-utilization peak. The text does qualify the latter as 'a traffic-level variant, not a new basis', so this is not a numerical contradiction; however, the phrase 'the one owned-fleet figure to quote' is ambiguous because it can be read as excluding the peak-fleet figure from all owned-fleet quoting. Clarify that the 6-host average is the default owned-fleet unit cost, while peak-fleet costs are separate capacity-provisioning figures.
fix_instruction: Replace 'The one owned-fleet figure to quote' with 'The default owned-fleet unit-cost figure to quote (average traffic, hour-matched basis)' and explicitly state that peak-fleet figures are separate provisioning costs, not alternative unit costs.

evidence: "Muse Glimmer 30B ([2°][FACT], source: vLLM-Recipes, citing the Meta model card) is a dense 29.6B local-agentic model that runs in ~18 GB at ~5-bit weights [2°]."
issue: Trailing bare [2°] tag is an Axis-1 label without its required Axis-2 companion. The Preface (page xv) states explicitly: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]" and "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair." The quantity "~18 GB at ~5-bit weights" is load-bearing and carries only Axis 1.
fix_instruction: Replace the trailing "[2°]" with a complete two-axis label pair, e.g. "[2°][FACT]" (if the value is stated by the vLLM-Recipes source) or "[2°][DERIVED]" (if the book derived it from model-card numbers).

evidence: PDF p.148 (printed p.124), figure text: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". Caption on the same page: "...while 1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget — a superset of TTFT violations...". Ch 4 (PDF p.110, printed p.86) states the opposite terminology: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
issue: The in-figure axis label calls the 2-second line the "TTFT budget", contradicting both the figure's own caption and the book's load-bearing SLO terminology (1.2 s = TTFT design budget; ≤2 s = p95 ceiling). A reader reading the figure alone will take the SLO as a 2 s budget rather than a p95 ceiling that relaxes a 1.2 s budget, and the label is doubly wrong because the line is drawn on the request-latency axis while named for TTFT (request latency ≥ TTFT, which the caption itself notes flags a superset of violations).
fix_instruction: Change the in-figure label from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s" (or "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)"), so the figure label matches the caption's terminology and the Ch 4 definition; add a note that the line is drawn on request latency, not TTFT.

evidence: PDF p.31 (printed p.8): "The vLLM FP8-KV blog post's often-quoted '54%' — from its Llama-3.1-8B Table 3 (vLLM blog, post dated 2026-04-22 ... ) [S6] — is, on this book's reading of that table, a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient [2°][HYPOTHESIS]." PDF p.155 (printed p.131), Ch 6 §6.6: "The vLLM FP8-KV blog's '54%' [S6] is a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient — on this book's own reading of that post's Table 3, not a vendor-stated interpretation [1P][HYPOTHESIS]; re-verify it against the post, as Ch 1 does at its KV-cache section."
issue: The identical claim, drawn from the identical source key [S6], carries two different Axis-1 provenance tags: [2°] in Ch 1 and [1P] in Ch 6. The book's Preface makes Axis 1 non-optional and says a label pair always takes one item from each axis ("[1P] — first-party: the model vendor's own spec" vs "[2°] — reputable second-hand"); a reader cannot tell whether the vLLM blog is first-party for this claim or second-hand, and the two chapters disagree on the evidence class of a load-bearing interpretation that Ch 7's FP8-KV accounting depends on.
fix_instruction: Pick one provenance for the '54%' interpretation and make it identical in Ch 1 §1.1.5, Ch 6 §6.6 and any Ch 7 restatement — e.g. [1P][HYPOTHESIS] if the vLLM post is treated as first-party for its own Table 3, or [2°][HYPOTHESIS] if the reading is the book's second-hand interpretation of a third party's table — and add a one-line note in the Sources chapter recording the choice.

evidence: PDF p.75 (printed p.51): "It is not the largest KV constant in the book: Ch 7 §7.4 re-derives the per-token value for other geometries, where a 100-layer, 12,288-hidden model at FP16 gives ~4.9 MB/token." Preface, PDF p.23 (printed p.ix): "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." and "§ N.M ... means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4". Ch 1 (PDF p.31) cites the same chapter differently: "the standing FP8-KV qualifiers are consolidated in Ch. 7 §4 (the accounting-basis note)".
issue: "Ch 7 §7.4" is the malformed form the Preface explicitly forbids: per the book's own convention it reads as "Ch 7, Section 7, Subsection 4", a target that does not exist, and the same chapter is cited elsewhere as "Ch. 7 §4" for a different purpose (the accounting-basis note). It is therefore unresolvable as written and conflicts with the cross-reference in Ch 1 — the reader cannot tell whether the intended target is Ch 7 Section 4 or the fourth subsection of Ch 7 Section 3 (where the per-token value for other geometries would sit).
fix_instruction: Rewrite as "§ 7.3.4" if the target is the fourth subsection of Ch 7's Worked Example, or as "§ 7.4" if it is Chapter 7 Section 4 — never "Ch 7 §7.4" — and confirm the Ch 1 cross-reference ("Ch. 7 §4 (the accounting-basis note)") points at the same or a different section, describing each target's content unambiguously.

evidence: PDF p.111 (printed p.87): "on the wall-clock paid-occupancy basis ($87,600/mo — the same fleet paid for all 730 h/mo — ÷ the same month's ~57.4B input tokens, an active-hours (173.33 h) volume) the same volume gives ~655K input tokens per $1 — wall-clock spend over active-hours tokens, an hour-basis mismatch and not a 730-hour token rate."
issue: The operation as written is inverted relative to the stated result. $87,600 ÷ 57.4B = 1.53×10⁻⁶ tokens per dollar, not ~655K; the stated figure requires 57.4B ÷ $87,600 = 655,251 tokens per dollar. Elsewhere in the book the same style is used correctly in the opposite direction ("$87,600 ÷ 6,240K ≈ $14.04", spend ÷ volume = cost), so the reader has to reverse the expression himself to reconcile it. Since this bullet is the source of the ~655K figure carried into Table 4-1's economic row and the sidebar table's qualifier, the printed arithmetic should be unambiguous.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the clause as "the same month's ~57.4B input tokens ÷ $87,600 gives ~655K input tokens per $1", keeping the operation and the result in the same direction as the surrounding ~2.76M derivation (which is written tokens/s ÷ $/s).

evidence: PDF p.75 (printed p.51): "The model card [1P][FACT] ... is the Qwen4-architecture preview: 125B total / 6B active (plus a separate 51B of offloadable N-gram embedding parameters), 512 MoE experts (10 routed + 1 shared per token), and hybrid attention ... the weights that must be resident for Qwen are its total set, ~125 × 10⁹ params × 2 bytes/param ≈ 250 GB (plus the offloadable N-gram); of that total, only ~6 × 10⁹ params are read per batch-1 decode token, at 2 bytes/param = ~12 GB ... and the ~250 GB total (not the ~12 GB active working set) is what must be resident unless experts are explicitly offloaded."
issue: The parameter accounting is internally ambiguous on the number the chapter calls load-bearing for sharding decisions. "125B total ... (plus a separate 51B of offloadable N-gram embedding parameters)" can be read as 125B inclusive of the 51B (125B total) or as 125B excluding it (176B total); the next sentence then calls "its total set" 125B and adds "(plus the offloadable N-gram)", which implies the second reading, and the later "the ~250 GB total ... is what must be resident" implies the first. A reader cannot tell whether resident weights are ~250 GB or ~352 GB — and the ~250 GB figure is the one used to argue "the difference between fitting on one host and sharding across several".
fix_instruction: State the accounting once, unambiguously: e.g. "125B transformer parameters + a separate 51B of offloadable N-gram embedding parameters = 176B total, of which ~250 GB (the 125B transformer set) must be resident and the N-gram table is offloadable" — and adjust the "~250 GB total" and "~1/21 of Qwen's own total weight footprint (~250 GB → 12 GB)" sentences to match whichever reading is intended.

evidence: In-figure annotation on the rendered Fig 6.2 (PDF p.148, printed p.124) reads verbatim: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The caption on the same page correctly states the line is "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch. 4 (PDF p.110) fixes the terminology: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to", and Ch. 6 §6.3.1 (PDF p.147) repeats: "a ceiling above the 1.2 s design budget, not a second budget".
issue: The figure's internal annotation attaches the word "budget" to the 2 s line, directly contradicting the book's own load-bearing budget-vs-ceiling distinction that the surrounding text and the figure's own caption enforce (1.2 s = design budget; 2 s = p95 ceiling). A reader quoting the figure would misstate the SLO basis.
fix_instruction: Change the in-plot annotation from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)" (or "p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s"), keeping the caption unchanged. Then sweep all other figures/tables that plot the 2 s line (e.g., any Ch. 14/15 SLO plots) for the same mislabel.

chapter: Ch. 2 (What Actually Happens During Inference) — Table 2-2
evidence: Table 2-2 row (PDF p.52): "Prefill: input tokens | 9,200 | 1,200 prompt + 8K context [canonical scenario][DERIVED]". Table 4-2 row (PDF p.103) labels the identical quantity: "Input tokens | 9,200 (1,200 prompt + 8,000 retrieved) | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]", and Table 4-1's table-level provenance note (PDF p.90) states the convention: "an input or parameter assumption (traffic, latency target, price, token count) is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]".
issue: Provenance/epistemic-label inconsistency for a repeated load-bearing quantity: the canonical 9,200 input-token count is tagged [DERIVED] in Table 2-2 but [ASSUMPTION] in Tables 4-1/4-2, and the stated convention explicitly classifies token counts as assumptions. Under the book's own rule ("where this panel and that paragraph appear to differ, the stricter reading applies"), one of the two tags is wrong.
fix_instruction: Re-tag the Table 2-2 row "Prefill: input tokens" as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (or, if the sum 1,200 + 8,000 is meant to be DERIVED, state that convention explicitly and align Table 4-2's row). While fixing, verify the adjacent Table 2-2 row "Model params | 70B | canonical scenario (Ch 4, Table 4-2)", which appears in the text layer without the [ASSUMPTION] epistemic tag that Table 3-1 ("[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] reference model") and Table 4-2 give the same quantity.

chapter: Ch. 4 (The Anatomy of an AI Workload) — Note † (Table 4-1 economic row)
evidence: Note † (PDF p.99, printed p.75) states verbatim: "The 730-hour volume at the same 92,000 tok/s offered rate would be ~241.8B (92,000 × 3,600 × 730), so the two figures differ only in which hour count is used for the spend (730 h paid vs 173.33 h active), while the token volume is the same active-hours volume in both". The preceding sentence had fixed the token volume at "~57.4B input tokens (6.24M requests × 9,200 = 57.4B)".
issue: Non-sequitur / contradictory referent: the sentence first introduces a hypothetical 730-hour token volume (241.8B), then concludes with "so" that the token volume "is the same active-hours volume in both" (57.4B). The 241.8B figure is never used by the conclusion, and a naive read yields two different token volumes inside one argument. (The arithmetic itself checks: 92,000 × 3,600 × 730 = 241.78B; 57.4B/20,800 = 2.76M; 57.4B/87,600 = 655K.)
fix_instruction: Split into two sentences: (1) state that ~2.76M and ~655K divide the same 57.4B active-hours token volume by two different spend bases ($20,800 vs $87,600), differing only by the 730/173.33 = 4.21 hour-count ratio; (2) add the 241.8B figure as a separate caution, e.g. "a true 730-hour token rate would divide by ~241.8B (92,000 × 3,600 × 730), not 57.4B — do not read 655K as a 730-hour token rate."

evidence: "Qwen3.8-Flash-Next card states a native 262K-token window... GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M"
issue: The text cites model families (Qwen 3.8, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4) and specific architectural names (e.g., "N-gram embedding parameters" for Qwen, "Wan2.2 TI2V-5B" for video) that do not correspond to actual hardware models released by the respective vendors as of the 2026 timeframe implied by the book's internal logic. While the book explicitly labels these as "constructed reference models" or "teaching geometry" in the Preface, the text in Chapter 1, Section 1.1.2 presents them as "current frontier cards" with "[1P][FACT]" tags, implying they are real, verifiable vendor specifications. This creates a mismatch between the evidence label (Fact) and the content (Fiction/Hypothetical), confusing the reader about whether to look up these specs or if they are illustrative.
fix_instruction: Verify if these model names are intended to be treated as hypothetical for the book's scenario or if they are errors in the source data. If they are hypothetical, the `[1P][FACT]` tag must be replaced with `[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]` or similar, and the text should explicitly state these are constructed examples for calculation, not actual vendor cards. If they are real, verify the specifications against vendor documentation.
